item.title: Lifestyle Entrepreneurship: Challenges, Innovations, and Community Impact
item.content:encoded:
Lifestyle entrepreneurship represents a growing but fragmented research area that extends beyond traditional profit-maximization approaches to encompass quality of life, personal fulfillment, and work-life balance. These entrepreneurs prioritize autonomy and alignment with personal values while establishing ventures often in tourism, hospitality, crafts, and creative sectors, frequently in rural or low-density areas where they contribute to local economic development and cultural preservation.

Despite increasing recognition of its significance, existing research lacks an integrated perspective examining both entrepreneur characteristics and their operational ecosystems. Lifestyle entrepreneurs face persistent challenges including financial instability, seasonal market dependence, and insufficient institutional support, while contextual factors such as social networks, public policies, and cultural influences significantly shape their business structures and community interactions.

Appel publié par Journal of Enterprising Communities: People and Places in the Global Economy. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Profile of lifestyle entrepreneurs: sociodemographic characteristics, values and experiences
  • Motivations for lifestyle entrepreneurship: sense of belonging (roots) to the territory, maintaining the culture and traditions of the territory, quality of life, self-fulfillment, balance between personal and professional life
  • Contextual factors: impact of social networks, public policies, local entrepreneurial ecosystems and socioeconomic environment
  • Challenges faced: financial instability, lack of institutional support, technological and market barriers, lack of qualified human resources
  • Impact of lifestyle entrepreneurship on local development: job creation, stimulation of the circular economy and contribution to sustainability
  • Resilience and adaptation strategies: innovative and sustainable solutions adopted by entrepreneurs in territories
  • Comparative case studies between different regions and sectors

Timeline

  • October 31, 2026: Closing date for manuscript submissions

item.title: Exploring the Interplay of Entrepreneurial Emotion, Judgment, and Decision Making
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines how emotions influence entrepreneurial judgment and decision-making, particularly in community-based and localized ecosystems. While existing research has focused on positive emotions like passion and resilience, the issue seeks to explore understudied emotional domains such as despair, awe, humility, guilt, empathy, and regret that shape entrepreneurs' strategic choices, resilience, and ethical judgments.

The special issue welcomes interdisciplinary research on how diverse emotional experiences affect entrepreneurial cognition and behavior within small businesses, family firms, and social enterprises. It invites both quantitative approaches examining causal relationships and qualitative studies exploring contextualized experiences, alongside theoretical contributions offering new frameworks for understanding emotions in entrepreneurship.

Insights from this research aim to inform policy-making, entrepreneurial education, and support structures by revealing how emotional dynamics drive sustainable business practices, ethical decision-making, and community engagement in localized entrepreneurial ecosystems.
